title: Your Compliance Journey
subtitle: Follow these steps in order — each one unlocks the next. Think of it as your personal legal checklist.
step_locked_body: This step opens up once you finish the steps it depends on.
step_locked_plan_ahead_body: You can read what to bring, where to go, and how this step works right now. Finish {steps} first to take action.
action_locked_hint: Finish the steps this one depends on before marking it done.
next_step_locked_hint: Finish {steps} first to unlock this step.
step_food_safety_training_why: Required by law (R638). Inspectors ask for proof before issuing your Health Certificate.
step_cipc_why: Needed to open a business bank account, apply for the R500m fund, and get your trading permit.
step_sars_tax_why: Required by law if your shop earns income. Also needed for your trading permit and the government fund.
step_coa_why: Proves your shop meets food safety standards. Selling food without one can mean a fine or closure.
step_municipal_registration_why: Without this your shop is operating illegally and can be closed on the spot. Also required for the government fund.
step_uif_why: If you have staff working more than 24 hours per month, UIF is required by law.
step_smmesa_why: The government small-business registry — needed before you can apply for up to R300,000 from the R500m Spaza Shop Support Fund.
progress_fund_teaser: A few more steps and you could qualify for up to R300,000 in funding.
permit_requirements_fallback: We don't have the document list for your area yet. Bring your ID, proof of address, and any business documents you already have.
permit_docs_we_prepare: Documents we can prepare for you
coa_readiness_header: Is your shop ready for inspection?
coa_readiness_intro: Health inspectors check these when they visit. {passing} of {total} ready.
coa_requirements_fallback: Bring your ID, proof of address, and details of your shop. The Environmental Health office will tell you the rest.
coa_evidence_header: Bring this with you to the inspection
coa_no_fixed_expiry_note: Your Health Certificate doesn't have a fixed expiry date. You must re-apply if your shop address, ownership, or person-in-charge changes. Your municipality may also do routine annual re-inspections.
coa_processing_time_note: Processing typically takes 10 working days to 2 months depending on your municipality — plan around the inspector's site visit.
coa_display_requirement_note: Once issued, keep your Certificate of Acceptability visible to the public at the shop at all times (R638 requirement).
coa_how_header: How to get your Health Certificate
coa_how_step_1: Make sure your Food Safety Training (Step 1) is done — inspectors will ask
coa_how_step_2: Fix any issues in the readiness checklist above (clean surfaces, working fridge ≤5°C, no pests, covered bins)
coa_how_step_3: Print or download the application form from your municipality's website (link below)
coa_how_step_4: Go to your nearest Environmental Health office — bring your ID and the completed form
coa_how_step_5: An inspector will visit your shop. Once you pass, they issue the Certificate of Acceptability
permit_how_header: How to get your Trading Permit
permit_how_step_1: Collect all the documents in the 'What to bring' list below (this is the most common reason for delays)
permit_how_step_2: Get the affidavits stamped at your nearest police station — free, takes 10 minutes (templates below)
permit_how_step_3: Go to the municipal office listed under 'Where to go' — bring originals AND certified copies
permit_how_step_4: Submit and get a reference number. Processing typically takes 4–8 weeks
permit_how_step_5: Once approved: display the permit in your shop where customers and inspectors can see it
checklist_unknown_fallback: We don't have a checklist for this step in your area yet.
office_unknown_fallback: We don't have office details for {area} yet.
office_unknown_hint: Search 'environmental health [your area]' or call your municipality's customer care.
office_find_link: Find Environmental Health offices near you
form_bring_id_warning: Bring your ID/passport to fill in that field at the office.
form_bring_passport_warning: Bring your passport AND visa/permit originals to fill in those fields at the office.
visa_warning_title: Your trading permit is linked to your visa
visa_warning_body: If your visa or permit expires, your trading permit automatically becomes invalid. Always renew before it expires.
permit_foreign_visa_link_notice: Your trading permit is tied to your visa or permit. If your visa expires, the trading permit expires too — renew your visa first.
cipc_how_step_3_foreign: Enter your full name and passport number
cipc_how_step_1_foreign: Go to eservices.cipc.co.za and create a customer code (BizPortal's quick sign-up needs a South African ID, so use eServices instead)
cipc_foreign_note: As a foreign national you register through CIPC eServices using a certified copy of your passport. CIPC runs a 'Foreigner Assurance' identity check, so your registration is processed by hand and can take a little longer than the citizen self-service route.
sars_how_step_3_foreign: Enter your passport or asylum-seeker number and contact details
sars_foreign_note: SARS registers you based on your income in South Africa, not your immigration status — you can get a tax number using your passport or asylum-seeker number.
uif_how_step_3_foreign: Enter your company details and each employee's name, ID or passport, and salary
coa_how_step_4_foreign: Go to your nearest Environmental Health office — bring your passport and the completed form
step_cipc_why_foreign: Needed to open a business bank account and get your trading permit.
step_sars_tax_why_foreign: Required by law if your shop earns income. Also needed for your trading permit.
step_municipal_registration_why_foreign: Without this your shop is operating illegally and can be closed on the spot.
cipc_need_required_a_foreign: You want to trade as a registered company (Pty) Ltd
coa_requirements_fallback_foreign: Bring your passport, proof of address, and details of your shop. The Environmental Health office will tell you the rest.
permit_requirements_fallback_foreign: We don't have the document list for your area yet. Bring your passport and permit, proof of address, and any business documents you already have.
step_right_to_trade_why: As a foreign national, you need a valid visa or permit that allows you to run a business. Every other step depends on this.
rtt_what_body: To own and run a shop in South Africa as a foreign national, you need ONE of these:
rtt_permit_business: Business visa — for running your own business (Immigration Act)
rtt_permit_s24: Refugee permit (Section 24) — gives you the right to work and run a business
rtt_permit_s22: Asylum seeker permit (Section 22) — only if it is endorsed to allow work or business
rtt_permit_pr: Permanent residence — gives you almost the same trading rights as a citizen
rtt_no_status_body: You haven't recorded a visa or permit yet. Add it in Settings (Redo compliance check) so we can guide the rest of your journey correctly.
rtt_renew_note: Your municipal trading permit is tied to your visa or permit. If it expires, your trading permit falls away too — always renew before it expires.
rtt_fronting_title: Never register your shop in someone else's name
rtt_fronting_body: Registering your business under a South African's name — to get around the rules or reach the government fund — is called 'fronting'. It is a criminal offence under the B-BBEE Act: up to 10 years in prison or a fine of up to 10% of your turnover. Always register in your own name, with your own passport and permit.
doc_landlord_affidavit_desc: Movestock template, pre-filled with your shop address. Take it to a Commissioner of Oaths (police station — free) to be signed and stamped. There's no government-issued version — any sworn affidavit format works.
doc_goods_affidavit_desc: Movestock template. Sworn statement that you don't sell illegal goods. Pre-filled with your details. Get stamped at the police station.
official_form_pdf_body: Your municipality publishes a downloadable form for this step. Download it, then use Movestock's cheat sheet below to copy in your shop details.
official_form_portal_title: Apply via your municipality's online portal
official_form_portal_body: Your municipality accepts applications online — no PDF to print. Movestock's cheat sheet below shows the details you'll need to enter.
doc_compliance_report_desc: Shows your stock records, expiry tracking, and supplier info. Proves you're already managing your shop properly.
doc_evidence_pack_desc: Combines 30 days of your daily checklists, temperature logs, supplier records, and pest control into one report.
action_error_generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
staff_empty: You haven't added any staff yet. Add them in Manage Staff first.
staff_error_generic: Could not update. Please try again.
cipc_need_required_a: You want to apply for government funding
cipc_need_required_b: You want to separate personal and business finances
cipc_need_required_c: You want to open a business bank account
cipc_need_optional_a: You're a sole trader with no plans for formal funding
cipc_cost: Cost: R175 for a Private Company (Pty)
cipc_fund_callout: You said you're interested in the government fund — CIPC is required.
cipc_how_step_1: Go to bizportal.gov.za and create an account
cipc_how_step_3: Enter your full name and ID number
cipc_how_step_4: Pick a company name (or skip and use the registration number)
cipc_how_step_5: Enter your home address and shop address
cipc_how_step_7: Wait 1–3 business days for approval, then download your certificate
cipc_annual_return_note: After registration: file your Annual Return every year — R100 (Pty under R1m turnover) or R450 (over R1m). Must also submit a Beneficial Ownership Declaration. We'll remind you when it's due.
sars_no_data_yet: Most spaza shops qualify for Turnover Tax — a simpler system for businesses earning under R2.3 million per year.
sars_qualify_turnover_body: A simpler system for small businesses. One payment per year based on your total sales. Much easier than standard income tax.
sars_tax_free_band_note: The first R600,000 of turnover is tax-free under Turnover Tax — most spaza shops pay nothing. Above R600,000 the rate steps up to a maximum of 3% (cap: R39,500 per year at R2.3m turnover).
sars_above_threshold_title: You may need full SARS registration
sars_above_threshold_body: Your sales may be above the R2.3 million Turnover Tax threshold. Speak to a tax practitioner or SARS branch to register correctly.
sars_how_step_3: Enter your ID number and contact details
sars_how_step_4: Select 'Individual' (sole trader) or 'Company' (if you registered with CIPC)
sars_how_step_5: Apply for Turnover Tax (TT01) — much simpler than income tax
sars_how_step_6: Once registered, request your Tax Clearance Certificate via eFiling — you'll need this for your trading permit
sars_tax_clearance_note: Once registered, get your Tax Clearance Certificate. You'll need it for your trading permit.
uif_what_body: UIF protects your workers if they lose their jobs, get sick, or go on maternity leave. It's a safety net you pay into each month.
uif_who_must_register: Required for any employee who works more than 24 hours per month for you.
uif_cost: Cost: 2% of each employee's wages — you pay 1%, they pay 1%. Submitted by the 7th of each month.
uif_how_step_2: Click 'Register as Employer' and follow the prompts
uif_how_step_3: Enter your company details and each employee's name, ID, and salary
uif_how_step_4: Every month, submit your EMP201 declaration by the 7th of the month
food_what_layer_1: You (the owner / person in charge): accredited food safety training under R638.
food_what_layer_2: Any staff who handle food: basic food hygiene training.
food_what_note: The training must be from an accredited provider. It does not need to be SETA — any SAQA, FoodBev SETA, SAATCA, or HPCSA-accredited course qualifies.
food_option_online_desc: Self-paced course on your phone. Providers include ASC Food Safety (ascfoodsafety.com) and NSF (nsf.org/za).
food_option_virtual_desc: Live training with an instructor. More interactive, slightly more expensive.
food_option_inperson_desc: On-site training. Most expensive. Requires a minimum group size.
food_how_step_1: Choose a training provider from the options above
food_how_step_2: Complete the accredited food safety course (typically 1–2 days online or in person)
food_how_step_4: Mark this step as done and upload or note your certificate date below
food_how_step_5: Your staff also need basic hygiene training — mark each one as trained in the staff list below
food_owner_not_trained: You haven't logged your training yet.
food_keep_cert_note: Keep your training certificate yourself and show it to inspectors when asked — Movestock doesn't store documents.
smmesa_what_body: It's the government's small business registry, now run by SEDFA (the merged agency of SEDA, SEFA, and the Co-operative Banks Development Agency). You need to be registered here before applying for the R500m Spaza Shop Support Fund (up to R300,000 per shop).
smmesa_how_step_2: Create an account with your details
smmesa_how_step_3: Register your business and save the reference number
smmesa_apply_via_fund_portal: Once registered, apply for the fund itself at spazashopfund.co.za, or call the NEF call centre on 011 305 8080.
popia_body: If you keep any customer information — phone numbers, a credit list, or WhatsApp order records — you are covered by the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA). As the owner you are automatically the Information Officer. You must keep customer data secure and only use it for the purpose you collected it for. Visit inforegulator.org.za to register (it's free).
